review_notes: I read the whole target file and checked the related Trace.lean and CommutatorQuotient.lean uses by grep. I also read the test client K0TraceNaturalityClient.lean. The only clear repeated proof is the 8-line proof that f maps additive commutators into additive commutators. It appears twice in the target theorem, once in the statement and once in the proof. It appears a third time as a separate lemma in the tests. The other repetitions (the two `rw` calls on the generator, and the two `hom_ext` steps) are short or routine, so I did not report them. I could not compile the proposed lemma. Its statement is copied from the test lemma that already compiles, so I expect it to work.

findings.problem: The same proof of `Ring.additiveCommutators R ≤ (Ring.additiveCommutators S).comap f.toAddMonoidHom` is written out twice in this theorem. It appears once in the statement (lines 40-46) and once in the proof as the definition of `q` (lines 52-58). The argument unfolds the closure, uses `closure_le`, and shows that `f (a*b-b*a)` is a commutator. The statement therefore carries an inline tactic block, which makes the theorem hard to read. The proof must also re-state the same map, so a change to one copy has to be mirrored in the other. The test file `K0TraceNaturalityClient.lean` contains a third copy as `commutators_le_comap`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma before the theorem, in this file or next to `Ring.additiveCommutators` in `GeneralLinearGroups.AdditiveCommutator`. Its statement is `theorem Ring.additiveCommutators_le_comap {R S} [Ring R] [Ring S] (f : R →+* S) : Ring.additiveCommutators R ≤ (Ring.additiveCommutators S).comap f.toAddMonoidHom`. The proof is the existing 8-line block: unfold to `AddSubgroup.closure`, apply `(AddSubgroup.closure_le _).2`, `rintro x ⟨a, b, rfl⟩`, then `simpa only [map_sub, map_mul] using Ring.commutator_mem_additiveCommutators (f a) (f b)`. In the theorem, the statement becomes `QuotientAddGroup.map (Ring.additiveCommutators R) (Ring.additiveCommutators S) f.toAddMonoidHom (Ring.additiveCommutators_le_comap f) (traceModCommutators R z)`. The proof uses the same term in `let q := QuotientAddGroup.map ... (Ring.additiveCommutators_le_comap f)`. Better still, add `def commutatorQuotientMap (f : R →+* S) : (R ⧸ Ring.additiveCommutators R) →+ (S ⧸ Ring.additiveCommutators S)`. Then the statement reads `commutatorQuotientMap f (traceModCommutators R z)` and `q` disappears. The test file can then drop its private copy `commutators_le_comap` and use the shared lemma. The hypotheses are unchanged, because the lemma needs only `[Ring R] [Ring S]` and the file already has both.
findings.benefit: The statement of the main naturality theorem becomes readable. The closure argument is proved once and used in the statement, the proof and the tests. Later changes to the map on commutator quotients, such as functoriality lemmas for id and comp, then have one definition to reference instead of re-pasting the tactic block.
